name: coordination/refusal-already-dispatched
description:
The second half of the §5.2 explicit-decision invariant, on the admin side (ADR-0016 §3, §6). `stage_consent` refuses a staging the **dispatch ledger** says has already been dispatched — not merely one that still holds an unconsumed receipt. Without this the surface would mint a second one-shot authorization for a disclosure that had already been carried to a pinned peer and acknowledged by it, and would render the operator a risk card reading "staging was inert: nothing has left this machine yet" over exactly those bytes: the one moment the card exists to get right.

Refused rather than permitted-with-an-honest-card, for two reasons. A second consent could only authorize a second disclosure of the same staged digest, and `coord_dispatches` resolves a `stage_ref` to a single row — a second row would make `task_status` and `stage_show` ambiguous about which disclosure they describe. And the recovery an operator actually wants when carriage was not acknowledged is the driver's retry under the same `execution_key`, which spends nothing and re-carries the disclosure that already exists. So `detail` names that key and where its carriage got to, which is the whole of the operator's next step. `409`, not `403`: the operator was allowed to ask; there is simply nothing left to authorize.

problem.title: this staging has already been dispatched
problem.detail: consent for this staged digest was already spent under execution_key exec-0001 (carriage failed); re-present that execution_key to resume carriage, which spends nothing
